items.statement: Company generates INR 150-175 crores annual cash flow; Q1 cash generation close to INR 40 crores; negative working capital business with low cash requirements for growth.
items.quote: Even in the first quarter, our cash generation will be, I think, close to INR 40 crores. So we generate INR150 crores, INR175 crores in that range of cash every year.

items.statement: Management prefers returning cash via dividends rather than retaining in treasury given strong cash generation and low capex needs.
items.quote: We don't require that much cash. We are almost negative working capital business to some extent. So our cash requirements even to grow the business are not substantial. Then we feel it's better to reward our shareholders with a good dividend rather than keeping the cash in our treasury.

items.statement: Employee count grew from ~1,200 in 2019 to ~1,900 currently; ~80% increase due to lab expansion (10 to 30 labs), remainder from business development and phlebotomy network.
items.quote: If you go back to 2019, I think we had 10 labs. Today, we have 30 labs and that is largely the increase in employee cost, running 10 labs versus 30 labs.

items.statement: Competition and pricing pressure cooling down after post-COVID intensity; slab-based pricing implemented May 2023 well accepted by franchisees.
items.quote: The competition, I feel it's slowly, I think cooling down. I think initially, the impact post-COVID was definitely a lot of competition coming in and decreasing prices and trying to win the market. But as the non-COVID business has stabilized over the last couple of years, we are now seeing some cling -on effects of the pricing decrease that the competition was doing.

items.statement: Complaints per million samples reduced 70% year-on-year; 9 out of 10 doctors trust Thyrocare reports per independent study.
items.quote: On the quality front, this quarter, we have reduced our complaints per million samples by 70% against last year.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 250 crore for FY25 remains intact and includes hub expansion
items.quote: Yes it does include the expansion of the hub.

items.statement: Added 2-3 high capex intensive hubs in FY25; plans another 2-3 hubs depending on profitability
items.quote: And additionally, it would be another 2 to 3 or 3 to 4 depending upon the profitability, how we make our profits, and what would be the strategy for the next year.

items.statement: Guwahati sector inbound utilization at 75-80% vs optimum 85-90%; overall aircraft utilization 70-75% vs ideal 85-90%
items.quote: However, the inbound into Guwahati is around between 75% to 80% versus the benchmark of 85% to 90% being the optimum one.

items.statement: Expect Guwahati sector to reach break-even utilization from September festive season
items.quote: We expect this somewhere with our festives getting kicked off somewhere from September onwards.

items.statement: Margins pressured by surface growth outpacing air, merit increases, and hub depreciation; expect 2-3% improvement from current levels
items.quote: We expect the margins to improve by another, from the current level to another 2% to 3%.

items.statement: PBT margin outlook remains 7-8% with 10-12% revenue growth; no forward-looking statements given
items.quote: And with that perspective in our margins, we would like to, we still keep an outlook of decently between 7% to 8% margin percentage.

items.statement: Optimistic demand outlook driven by GDP growth, e-commerce and infrastructure improvement
items.quote: We are optimistic. We see as the GDP growth rates improve, the e-commerce, the infrastructure improves, we see healthy prospects.

items.statement: General price increase of 3.9-4% implemented across products selectively based on contracts
items.quote: We have had our general price increases. Of course, it is not to the expected budgeted level what we had, but roughly be tween 3.9% to 4% is the additional revenue that comes from

items.statement: Fuel cost neutralized via variable surcharge linked to Brent crude in customer contracts
items.quote: So, typically, our customers, our customer contracts have a fuel surcharge clause, which percentage increases or decreases based on the global Brent oil prices.

items.statement: No one-off costs in Q1; current costs expected to generate revenue or efficiencies in upcoming quarters
items.quote: It's a normal quarter a nd we expect those, against those costs, the additional revenue or efficiencies to be generated

items.statement: Merit increases of ~4% YoY and ~4.5-4.6% QoQ impacted margins
items.quote: So, normal merit increase roughly would be, we will have to, you know, it is roughly, you know, 4% Y-o-Y, you know, quarter-on-quarter increase, ma'am.

items.statement: Shipments grew 7.4% QoQ to 90.15 million; weight grew 9.6% QoQ to 313,089 tons
items.quote: Overall in terms of shipments, last quarter , it was 83.94 million shipments. This quarter, it is 90.15 million. In terms of weight, it is 285,643 tons in June 23 quarter. And it is 313,089 weight in tons in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Facing tough competition in surface express; aim for profitable growth with pricing flexibility for key customers
items.quote: On the surface part, we are growing more on the surface and on the surface, we are facing a very tough competition.

items.statement: Rate per shipment up 2.1% YoY; revenue per kg down 0.7% YoY
items.quote: Overall, at RPS, RPK level versus the previous year quarter, we are seeing a marginal growth on the RPS part and RPK slightly down. However, rate for shipment has increased by 2.1%, whereas RPK is 0.7% down.

items.statement: Margin expansion dependent on optimum aircraft utilization and domestic demand; no forward-looking statements provided
items.quote: We had said that, provided, we are able to generate that m uch level of, provided we go for an optimum utilization. I think that's the one. A is that, we do not make any forward -looking statement.

items.statement: Management maintains FY25 growth guidance of 75% and will not revise until half-yearly numbers
items.quote: I don't think I will change any guidance right now, but for sure, whatever you have calculated, it's there. I mean, it's right there and it's not going to be zero for sure. So, we are yet to arrive at it, but we don't want to revise anything at least until we have the half yearly numbers.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 180% YoY from Rs 7.8 crore to Rs 22 crore; EBITDA margin expanded 503 bps YoY and 255 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA has risen from about 7.8 crore to about 22 crore, which is again year-on-year growth of 180%, but when you see quarter-on-quarter, still we see 34% growth from Q4 last year to Q1 this year from about 44 crore to about 60 crore and which is again an increase of about 503 bps in the EBITDA percentage growth year-on-year as against Q-o-Q growth of about 255 bps.

items.statement: Per-transaction realization may drop 10-15% if government digital payment incentives removed, but volume growth expected to offset
items.quote: If you take it as one of the components, then for only one specific component, then for sure it will have an impact maybe, I don't know, maybe 10%, 15% approximately. But what is the volume that gets added to take away this impact? That is something that we need to go back and see.

items.statement: International business grew 17% YoY in Q1 FY25; demand side looks solid and positive trend in consumption expected to continue
items.quote: Going forward, we see the positive trend in terms of consumption, demand side looks solid, and we see good in terms of demand side.

items.statement: Gross profit margin declined 30 bps YoY to 33.5% due to increased input costs
items.quote: Gross profit grew by 16% and gross profit margin was 30 bps lower from 33.8% to 33.5% on account of increase in input costs.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stood at 12.4% in Q1 FY25, up 15% YoY in absolute terms
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter 1 was higher by 15% on a year-on-year basis at INR258 crores compared to INR224 crores last year and the EBITDA margin stood at around 12.4%.

items.statement: Logistics costs as percentage of revenue increased 1.5% YoY and 1.6% QoQ due to Red Sea crisis impact on freight
items.quote: Logistic costs as percentage to revenue have increased by 1.5%.

items.statement: Freight costs expected to remain elevated for 1-2 more quarters; July rates slightly higher than Q1 average
items.quote: July will be a little higher.

items.statement: Company partially passed on freight cost increases to customers but strategically avoids full pass-through as it views the impact as temporary
items.quote: Because this is a temporary and as strategically, we don't want to pass it on to the customer. For some part, we have done it. In some part, we have not done it.

items.statement: Investing INR87 crores (USD10 million) to double retort ready-to-eat capacity in US; UK facility capex of GBP65 million already commissioned
items.quote: So the two -- the capex is -- one is we are doubling our capacity in U S for our -- this retort business, ready-to-eat business. So that will be roughly INR87 crores, USD10 million we are investing there to pu t capacity.

items.statement: US retort ready-to-eat capacity being doubled due to demand exceeding current capacity
items.quote: We have more demand than the capacity we have.

items.statement: UK facility commissioned with processing and packaging capabilities; expected to generate USD40 million revenue in first year
items.quote: And we have set up this facility which is all processing and packaging facilities. So we are expecting in this year USD40 million revenue.

items.statement: Jasmine rice sales volume approximately 70,000 tons annually; all manufacturing outsourced to Thailand millers
items.quote: So sales capacity we sell roughly 70,000 tons. As far as the manufacturing, that is all outsourced and we buy from the Thailand millers.

items.statement: Organic staples portfolio estimated at INR700-800 crores market size in India; launching soon
items.quote: Nielsen doesn't cover that, but estimate is roughly INR700 crores to INR800 crores organic the complete portfolio as a market.

items.statement: Appointed strong distributor in Saudi Arabia (1.2M ton Basmati market); Middle East currently 8% of revenue but key focus for next growth phase
items.quote: Middle East contribute roughly 8%. But as far as Saudi is concerned, we have appointed our partner there, distributor for that market.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced by 8 days to 202 days YoY through continued optimization focus
items.quote: Because of our continued focus on the working capital optimization, our net working capital days have also reduced by 8 days to 202 days versus 210 days in the last quarter, in the last quarter 1 financial year '24.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity improved to 0.2x from 0.4x; debt-to-EBITDA improved to 0.8x from 1.2x YoY; targeting further deleveraging in FY25
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio declined from 0.4x to 0.2x, and the debt-to-EBITDA ratio for quarter 1 financial '25 is 0.8 versus 1.2 in the previous corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Insurance claim of ~INR160 crores plus interest expected within 4 weeks per Supreme Court order; Golden Star earnout payment due June 2025
items.quote: Supreme Court has said that within 4 weeks we should get our money with Bank guarantee. So that's good news and we will get our money in 4 weeks' time.

items.statement: Kharif season sowing 10-15% higher than last year with good monsoon; expecting larger crop and lower commodity prices
items.quote: So whatever the forecast we are getting the crop is sowing is more 10% to 15% against last year and the monsoon is good. So everything so far is looking good and we are expecting more crop, lesser price.

items.statement: Premiumization expected to drive 0.5-0.7% margin expansion from higher gross margin products
items.quote: We have given the guidance also that where our margin expansion will come. We said 0.5% to 0.7% will come from premiumization.

items.statement: Commodity price decline impacted margins by 0.5-0.75% in Q1; 90% of crop now hedged for balance of year
items.quote: Overall I will say it may have impacted our margin by 0.5% or 0.75% down in this quarter.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat/ready-to-cook business in India expected to break even in FY26-27 at INR400 crores revenue base
items.quote: It will be breakeven in '26, '27. So on a revenue base of INR400 crores it will be and we are projecting that revenue to be in '26, '27.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement in FY25-26 as commodity prices decline and freight costs stabilize
items.quote: We are very optimistic on year '25, '26 as the prices of commodity will also come down and there will be a stability in the freight cost also.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis freight impact not yet behind; worst expected to last 1-2 more quarters
items.quote: No, the worst is not yet behind. We have seen the Red Sea impact a little bit and that's why the growth in the margin has impacted. But we are positive that this is only a quarter or 2 -quarter thing.

items.statement: Lower MEP on rice exports benefits industry; limited direct impact on LT Foods as it exports higher-value Basmati
items.quote: As far as the lowering down the M EP, the industry will definitely gain. As far as LT is concerned LT has not much impact on this because we are exporting on a higher value.

items.statement: Basmati and non-Basmati markets don't cannibalize; different geographies and income segments
items.quote: So if you see the Basmati market, they don't cannibalize with non-Basmati to Basmati. Non-Basmati is more Africa and the country with a lower income. But as far as Ba smati is concerned, that's mainly consumed in Middle East, Europe and America.

name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Limited

items.statement: Guided revenue and earnings growth of 30% to 35% for FY25
items.quote: With our strong performance in Q1, and a positive outlook for the upcoming quarters, we feel we are well placed to deliver on our guided growth of 30 % to 35% on revenue and earnings.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs. 1000+ Cr with 70% executable in 12 months and 90% in 18 months
items.quote: So, order book in terms of duration, it is roughly, I would say 85% to 90% of the order book will consume over 18 months. I would say 70 odd percent would come over 12 months.

items.statement: Order book split 65% TIG and 35% Banking; expected to grow 5-15% in Q2
items.quote: Right now, the split is most 65:35 in terms of the order book with TIG something in the range of 65% and banking something in the range of 35%.

items.statement: Margins to stay flat for next 2-3 years as R&D investment increases; long-term target 40-50% EBITDA
items.quote: So, the game plan is for the next two, three years to not focus on margin expansion. I don't think this is the time for Aurionpro to do it.

items.statement: Data center services capture 30-50% of project CAPEX depending on contract scope
items.quote: Most of the contracts is include design and program management thing you are getting to probably 30%, 35%, 40% of the spend. But you would never get to the 100% of the spend overall.

items.statement: TIG mix shifting: Data center and Transit growing strongly, Smart City shrinking
items.quote: And this year, data center will grow stronger than the TIG overall growth number, transit will go stronger than the TIG overall growth number and smart cities will shrink, will not grow.

items.statement: US revenue expected to grow 50-60% in FY25 to mid-teens million USD
items.quote: We expect this year US to get to let's say a double digit million dollar , more around the mid-teens number which should be a strong growth.

items.statement: Acquired Arya.AI to build global enterprise AI for banking and insurance; integration underway
items.quote: We concluded the acquisition of Arya.AI, which is again a game changer for our strategy to create a global enterprise AI player that is sharply focused on creating the next generation of AI offerings for banks and insurers globally.

items.statement: AS Software (Omnifin) acquired for retail SME lending gap; targeting global expansion in SE Asia and Middle East
items.quote: So, lending as you know, we have been very strong on the corporate loan origination side , collateral management, limit management, et cetera , we did not have an offering on the retail SME digital lending space. That's where AS 's Omnifin fits in.

items.statement: Received final RBI authorization for online payment aggregator license (AuroPay)
items.quote: We are also pleased to announce that we have received final authorization from RBI on the online payment aggregators.

items.statement: AuroPay focused on high-margin embedded payments (software + payments), not commoditized B2C gateway
items.quote: So, we will try to first build a business around spaces that we are strong in , transit payments where we own the contract end-to-end, this becomes a fantastic lever for margin expansion in those businesses because we have been using third party gateways anyway.

items.statement: Successfully concluded QIP with participation from prominent global and Indian institutions
items.quote: We concluded a succe ssful QIP and it's very encouraging to attract prominent global and Indian institutions to join us in this mission to create a global tech player rooted in India.

items.statement: Transit business has strong global pipeline across US, Latin America, Australia, UK via MasterCard and Vix partnerships
items.quote: So, we see a very strong pipeline on the transit side, it will certainly grow very strongly this year.

items.statement: AMC revenue streams are sticky, permanent, indexed at 3.5-4.5% annually; not included in order book but in guidance
items.quote: So, your stream would probably go up between, let's say, 3.5% to 4.5% or so every year because of being indexed to CPI and stuff like that.

items.statement: Sales channel doubled in last year; sales & marketing spend kept below 5% of revenue
items.quote: So, we typically keep it below 5%. For us, having said that the channel is now twice the size it was last year.

items.statement: Aurobees SME platform is a 3-5 year play; not a meaningful revenue contributor currently
items.quote: But I would say this is a three to five year play , don't expect a meaningful revenue contribution this year or the next.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% annual AUM growth and aims to double AUM every 3-4 years
items.quote: we still continue to maintain our growth trajectory of 20%-25%.

items.statement: Expects housing finance subsidiary to grow around 35% in foreseeable future
items.quote: we anticipate it to register a growth of around 35% in foreseeable future.

items.statement: Aims to maintain 25% of AUM off-book via direct assignment and co-lending
items.quote: We aim to maintain around 25% of the AUM as off-book through direct assignment and co-lending.

items.statement: Targets ROA range of 2.75% to 3.25% and NIMs close to 7%
items.quote: We should maintain our ROA in the range of 2.75% to 3.25%.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM reached INR 11,006.72 crores in Q1 FY25, up 24.12% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the exact number is INR 11,006.72 crores of AUM, and profit after tax is INR72.56 crores as on June '24, as compared to INR8,867.94 crores AUM and INR57.56 crores of PAT in June'23, which is 24.12% growth in AUM and 26.06% growth in PAT on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Standalone AUM grew 23.35% YoY to INR 10,383 crores
items.quote: our AUM grew by 23.35% from INR8,418 crores to INR10,383 crores.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle loans grew 82.28% YoY to INR 817 crores
items.quote: Commercial vehicle loan grew by 82.28% that is from INR448 crores to INR817 crores.

items.statement: Salaried personal loans grew 95% YoY to INR 590 crores
items.quote: And SPL loan, Salaried Personal Loan grew by 95% from INR303 crores to INR590 crores.

items.statement: Housing finance AUM grew 38.44% YoY to INR 623 crores
items.quote: AUM grew by 38.44% from INR450 crores to INR623 crores.

items.statement: Has INR 2,200 crores sanctions on hand for term loan, direct assignment and co-lending
items.quote: the company as on 30th June 2024 has sanctions on hand to a tune of INR2200 crores in the form of term loan, direct assignment and co-lending.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing stable at 9.80% in Q1 FY25 vs 9.65% YoY; expects it to remain stable
items.quote: The cost of borrowing for the quarter was 9.80%. The cost of borrowing for June quarter last year was 9.65%. If you compare with March number, it has remained stable. We expect the cost of borrowing to remain stable going forward too.

items.statement: Overall portfolio yield is around 17%
items.quote: So overall yield on the AUM is around 17%.

items.statement: Targets borrowing cost reduction of 20-30 bps but expects stability due to rising MCLR
items.quote: though we expect that this cost of borrowing to come down from 25 basis to 30 basis point, but the other way we have to see also that banks MCLR are also increasing. So, keeping in mind, therefore, we are into a trajectory where we see that it should be stable.

items.statement: Consolidated Gross Stage 3 at 2.29%, Net Stage 3 at 1.52%; management overlay of INR 17.60 crores (0.22% of on-book assets)
items.quote: Portfolio quality remained stable and strong at 2.29% Gross Stage 3 asset and Net Stage 3 asset is 1.52% as compared to 2.25% Gross Stage 3 and 1.51% Net Stage 3 as on March '24. We still carry a management overlay of INR17.60 crores as on June 24, which is 0.22% of our on-book assets.

items.statement: Housing finance Gross Stage 3 at 0.90%, Net Stage 3 at 0.65%; management overlay of INR 3 crores (0.63% of on-book assets)
items.quote: the gross stage 3 asset is 0.90% and net stage 3 asset is 0.65% as compared to 0.90% gross stage 3 and 0.66% net stage 3 as on March 24. Here also, we carry a management overlay of INR3 crores, which is 0.63% of our on-book assets.

items.statement: Current portfolio 0.6% below anticipated due to collection limitations from elections and heat wave; expected to recoup in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: if you see our current portfolio is somewhat around 0.6% less than what you would have anticipated. It has nothing to reflect on the deterioration on credit quality. It is just because of some limitations on efforts on collections because of elections and heat wave, which will be well recouped now, or it has already started recouping now.

items.statement: Plans to increase direct distribution share from 65% to 70-75% of AUM over next 3-4 years
items.quote: when we double our AUM, what looks like 65% through our direct distribution should be around 70-75% through our direct distribution, and 25-30% through our indirect distribution.

items.statement: Expanding geographic footprint into South (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, AP/Telangana) and North India
items.quote: South and North as well. So Southern states will start contributing meaningfully. Omkar Kamtekar: Any specific state that you are targeting or is it just a blanket? Dhvanil Gandhi: The three bigger states, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and AP Telangana. These are the three states where we have started setting up our foothold and footprint and these are the three Southern states that we will be focusing ri

items.statement: MSME segment contributed 62% of growth; practically all MSME borrowers are Udyam registered
items.quote: Practically each and every borrower that we serve in MSME is Udyam registered.

items.statement: Wheels portfolio (used CV, used cars, 2-wheelers) targeted at 25% of total portfolio; industry growing at 19-20%
items.quote: we have already shared that we want wheels to be around 25% of our portfolio going forward. And if you take some of the CRISIL surveys, we see next 5 years wheels growing at this large market of vehicles anywhere around 19% to 20%.

items.statement: Salaried personal loans capped at less than 10% of portfolio
items.quote: the key contributor will be the SME, the affordable housing, the wheels, and to an extent, salaried personal loan within a cap of less than 10%.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle pricing ranges 16-21% depending on model/geography/tenure; average 19-20%
items.quote: If we give the range, it can start from 16%, 17% to around 20%, 21% depending upon the models and the geographies and the tenure that are given. But on an average, we are in a position to get around 19% to 20%.

items.statement: Salaried personal loan customers require CIBIL score >700
items.quote: It will be more than 700. That is one of the criteria what we have kept. And even in our assessment standards, we have seen that the ones scoring less than 700 are not rendered eligible as per our credit assessment.

items.statement: Raised INR 500 crores equity via QIP (first since IPO); capital adequacy 28.59%, Tier-1 25.39%, debt/equity 3.08x
items.quote: As you all know, during the quarter, the company raised INR500 crores equity through QIP. This QIP marked the first equity raised by company since its IPO in 2017. The capital adequacy remains strong at 28.59% for the quarter, with Tier-1 capital of 25.39% and debt equity of 3.08 times.

items.statement: Raised INR 490 crores term loans (3-5 yr maturity) and INR 150 crores NCDs in Q1; has INR 725 crores term loan sanctions on hand
items.quote: We raised around INR490 crores term loan during the quarter, having an average maturity of 3 to 5 years. We further have around INR725 crores term loan sanctions on hand. In terms of capital market transaction, we raised INR150 crores NCD during the quarter.

items.statement: Average cash and equivalents of INR 800 crores (excl. QIP); unutilized CC facilities of INR 600 crores; CC utilization 70-75%
items.quote: company through its efficient liability management was able to maintain an average cash and cash equivalent of around INR800 crores excluding the QIP proceeds of INR500 crores and unutilized cash credit facilities of around INR600 crores.

items.statement: Quarterly portfolio runoff of INR 2,000-2,500 crores
items.quote: Every quarter run down is between INR2,000 crores to INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Advocates for MSME NPA reclassification from 90 to 180 DPD; expects some DPD recalibration (0.5-0.6%) as direct retail scales
items.quote: Currently there was a lot of demand from the MSME segment, especially to reclassify their definition of NP A from 90 to 180, as such as an industry body of N BFC, we have been advocating this since long. But having said that, within that 90 DPD bucket, there can be some recalibration, maybe of 0.5% or 0.6% here or there, but nothing to reflect on the credit quality or any stress on the assets
